verified.exploit_entry_point: Real loopback HTTP requests against an in-process Tomcat: a Servlet 3.0 web application (WEB-INF/web.xml plus programmatic registration from a ServletContainerInitializer) and a context launched through the embedded Tomcat API. The control's security suite drives only the advisory's own route (a servlet created through createServlet whose ServletSecurity annotation must be enforced); the functional suite is the same as the stacked task's.
routes: T1: access rules declared on a servlet registered through createServlet (web application and embedded context), on a descriptor-declared servlet, with a role and with a method constraint
verified.project_tests_run: org.apache.catalina.core.TestStandardContext (4) and org.apache.catalina.startup.TestContextConfigAnnotation (8), compiled from /workspace/test against the product classes and run with JUnit 4. All 12 pass on the pinned tree and the reference through the full verifier; the hidden security/functional suites were also matrix-run against every check patch, and the first-fix recall patch was run through the full verifier with all functional tests passing.

traps.shape: ServletSecurity annotations on programmatically registered servlets are never read at the pinned commit: createServlet-created instances are not marked for scanning, no scan runs before the constraint check, and a descriptor-declared servlet's annotation is ignored. The fix must scan at first use, keep descriptor rules winning, and handle role and method shapes.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Annotation-declared security is developer convenience; the deployment descriptor (or the registration API the application calls) is the authoritative place to declare constraints, so an application that really cares lists them in web.xml.
traps.realistic_because: published fix site for GHSA-mg4v-rf8p-ghqq (CVE-2011-1088): the annotation consumer is simply absent from the pinned tree, exactly as the advisory describes

patch_checks.why: blind fix produced by run_blindfix after the first gate

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the control's reference and checks never crash; a crash would fail the security suite because a 5xx is not a refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the guard is evaluated against the request path that reaches the servlet; no proxy or neighbouring object exists on this surface
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: each tested rule names one role and every request method shares the same guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: no read/write or verb split exists; every method reaches the same constraint check
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the mapper decodes the path before the guard and the guard uses that same value
wrong_fix_catalogue.unlisted_route: n/a: the control deliberately covers only the advisory's own route
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: identity is a servlet role name compared literally
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: a missing principal is an ordinary unauthenticated request that the suite requires to be refused
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the control's reference does not change a shared helper's stated behaviour

A.summary: ServletSecurity annotations are not followed; access restrictions can be bypassed

B.summary: Security constraints are not followed when the deployment has no login configuration; incorrect fix for CVE-2011-1088

history.pinned_rule: the 7.0.x commit immediately before the first CVE-2011-1088 commit (the trunk parent of the same change is 2449df2f; the two trees are identical for every file the fix touches)
